authored_explainer.title: Cereal Production Is 1.5x Higher Than In 1972
authored_explainer.hook: Cereal production rose 1.5x instead of running out.
says: Progression to secondary school rose from 77.8% in 1985 to 91.3% in 2017 — 1.2 times higher.
Cereal production climbed from 1083.7 million metric tons in 1972 to 1644.1 million metric tons in 2024 — 1.5 times higher.
China leads at 5.2 million square kilometers of farmland, then the United States at 4.2 million, Australia at 3.6 million, Brazil at 2.4 million, and Russia at 2.2 million.
authored_explainer.closing: Production kept rising while farmland remained concentrated.
authored_explainer.question: Which number changed your view?

authored_explainer.title: Combustible Renewables And Waste Is 3.0x Higher Than In 1990
authored_explainer.hook: Combustible renewables and waste tripled since 1990.
says: Combustible renewables and waste rose from 10.2% of total energy in 1990 to 30.1% in 2024 — 3.0 times higher.
Access to electricity rose from 73.2% of population in 1998 to 91.9% in 2024 — 1.3 times higher.
Methane (CH4) emissions from waste rose from 903.8 Mt CO2e in 1972 to 1,652 Mt CO2e in 2024 — 1.8 times higher.
authored_explainer.closing: More energy from waste also means more methane emissions.
authored_explainer.question: Which number surprised you most?

authored_explainer.title: Population Growth Fell 54% Since 1972
authored_explainer.hook: Population growth fell 54% instead of accelerating forever.
says: Rural population fell from 63.1% of total population in 1972 to 42.2% in 2025 — down to 67 percent of that.
Population in the largest city shifted from 18.2% of urban population in 1972 to 16.2% in 2025 — it barely moved.
Population growth fell from 2 annual % in 1972 to 0.91 annual % in 2025 — down to 46 percent of that.
authored_explainer.closing: The planet is still growing. It has just almost stopped accelerating.
authored_explainer.question: Which shift surprised you most?
